source.title: Strong Model Collapse
source.authors: Elvis Dohmatob; Yunzhen Feng; Arjun Subramonian; Julia Kempe

record.file_problem: The main paper and most appendices are present, but the text ends partway through Appendix G.2. The central claims and experiments are included.
record.tranche_reason: It reports test-error or test-loss outcomes while varying model width or depth, but in a synthetic-data/model-collapse setting rather than a direct reproduction of the original double-descent experiments.
record.gate_note: The study varies model size and reports test error/loss in random-projection models, MNIST networks, and GPT-2 models. Figure-only curves are recorded as such; their plotted numerical values are not recoverable from the supplied text. Sample-size curves about synthetic-data mixing are not rows for V3 because the text does not establish that they test whether more samples raise test error near an interpolation threshold. The double-descent statement in Figure 2 concerns the bias component, not a text-described test-error curve.
record.test_reason: The study sweeps random-projection width (λ=1e-8, n=500) and reports test error on the true distribution. It states that test error diverges at the interpolation threshold m=n and that larger models fare better past that point. This is a model-wise double-descent result in a new setting, training on a real+synthetic mixture, for random-feature regression rather than deep networks. The MNIST and GPT-2 size comparisons are too coarse to show the curve's shape.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. One addition: the authors claim their theory predicts a double-descent curve for model collapse itself. Note also that Section 4.2 describes the GPT-2 result inconsistently with the abstract on whether larger models amplify collapse before or after the interpolation threshold.
record.recipe_differences: The study combines theoretical and empirical model-size sweeps with real/synthetic data mixtures; it does not reproduce the original clean-data double-descent setup. It also studies collapse severity as well as test error.
record.method_sensitivity: Model-size effects vary with synthetic-data quality and proportion; the GPT-2 depth comparison changes with training-token count. The MNIST model-size result is reported for models remaining in the interpolation regime.

fits_no_version.finding: Model size changes the severity of model collapse. Larger models amplify it below the interpolation threshold and may mitigate it beyond.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Model collapse from synthetic data itself follows a double-descent profile in model size.

record.problems: The evidence is primarily about synthetic-data-induced model collapse rather than the unqualified double-descent claim. The supplied text does not give numerical values for the plotted size-sweep curves, and several reported comparisons do not establish the complete curve shape or interpolation-peak location. The MNIST width result is stated to remain in the interpolation regime.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 1 is a Pareto comparison of mixed-data and real-only test error rather than a direct text-described test-error curve against model size. Figure 2's explicit double-descent description concerns the bias component, not the total test-error curve. Figures 3 and 7 and the sample/token-scaling plots are omitted because they do not test the specified model-size or near-interpolation sample-size versions. The supplied Figure 4 text lists its plotted proportions but not the mapping of each individual curve to a plotted value; the corresponding conditions are retained in aggregate rows r01-r24.

untested.parts: No deep-network width sweep resolves a peak at the interpolation threshold. The MNIST and GPT-2 comparisons use few sizes and figure-only values.
No test of more samples raising error near the threshold.
Regularization is fixed near zero and label noise is not varied. There is no test of peak splitting or of removal under tuned regularization.

missing.what: Total test error E_test against width m for c2 ∈ {0, 0.1, 0.5, 1}, diverging at m=n=500. The reader excluded this as 'bias only', but the fourth panel is total test error and the text says all terms diverge at m=n.
Pareto comparison over parametrization rate ψ: under low-quality synthetic data the optimal model size is intermediate.

record.verdict_notes: Neither original source is this study. The core double-descent evidence is in the random-feature model (extending Bach 2023), not in deep networks. There is no V1 verdict because the deep-network rows cannot show the curve shape.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not report a complete, text-described test-error fall-rise-fall curve across model size with a peak located near the size that just fits the training set.
No test-error sweep over training epochs or training time.
No reported test of increasing training-sample count near an interpolation threshold to see whether test error rises.
The study does not establish that risk improves past interpolation generally across model classes; its experiments use particular regression, MNIST, and language-model settings.
No single effective-complexity measure is tested as predicting peak location across size, epochs, and samples.

The study varies synthetic-data quality and proportion, but does not test whether label noise or variance drives double descent, whether peaks split, or whether optimally tuned regularization removes them.
No test of whether counting complexity by an effective parameter measure turns the second descent into an ordinary U-shaped curve.
